title: Review: Aldehydes and ketones; Concentration and standard solutions; Indicators
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AM03#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR17b#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR17b#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR17b#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AB08#N.3a, AM03#N.9, OR17b#N.8, AB08#N.7a, AM03#N.7, OR17b#N.13, AB08#N.10a, AM03#N.11, OR17b#N.5, AB08#N.8, AM03#N.3a. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Standard solution
items.clue: Prepared by accurate weighing so that its concentration is accurately known.

items.label: Aldehyde
items.clue: Has an H on the C=O carbon, so mild oxidising agents turn it into a carboxylic acid.

items.label: Tollens' reagent
items.clue: Freshly made from AgNO₃(aq), a drop of NaOH(aq) and dilute NH₃(aq); warmed in a water bath.

items.label: Silver mirror
items.clue: Shiny metallic coating on the tube, formed as Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag: the positive result of the test.

questions.stem: An indicator, HInd, has pKa = 3.7: HInd(aq) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + Ind⁻(aq). HInd is red and Ind⁻ is yellow. What colour does the indicator show in a solution of pH 6.0, and why?

options.text: Yellow, as Ind⁻ predominates when the pH is above the pKa.
Red, as the solution is acidic, with its pH below 7.
Red, as HInd predominates when the pH is above the pKa.
Orange, as HInd and Ind⁻ are equal at equilibrium.

questions.explanation: At pH 6.0, [H⁺] = 1 × 10⁻⁶ mol dm⁻³, far below Ka = 2 × 10⁻⁴, so the equilibrium lies to the right: [Ind⁻]/[HInd] ≈ 200. The colour is yellow.

questions.stem: A student adds 600.0 cm³ of water to 200.0 cm³ of 0.500 mol dm⁻³ NaCl(aq), giving 800.0 cm³ of solution. What is the concentration of NaCl in the diluted solution, in mol dm⁻³?

A compound gives an orange precipitate with 2,4-DNPH. After recrystallising, the derivative melts at 154–156 °C. The compound gives no silver mirror with Tollens' reagent. Melting points of 2,4-DNPH derivatives: propanal 155 °C · propanone 126 °C · butanal 123 °C · pentan-3-one 156 °C. What is the compound?

options.text: Propanal
Propanone
Butanal
Pentan-3-one

questions.explanation: The melting point fits, and a ketone gives no mirror. Melting point alone could not separate it from propanal.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ ethanoic acid (pKa = 4.76) is titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ NaOH(aq) at 298 K. Three indicators are available, with these pH ranges: methyl orange 3.1–4.4; bromothymol blue 6.0–7.6; phenolphthalein 8.3–10.0. Which choice of indicator, with its reason, is correct?

options.text: Phenolphthalein, as the salt CH₃COONa makes the equivalence pH above 7.
Methyl orange, as its range is close to the pKa of ethanoic acid.
Bromothymol blue, as the equivalence point of a titration is at pH 7.
Any of the three, as the pH passes through every range near equivalence.

questions.explanation: At equivalence the flask holds sodium ethanoate; CH₃COO⁻ + H₂O ⇌ CH₃COOH + OH⁻ makes it basic (about pH 8.7). Phenolphthalein's range lies within the steep section.

questions.stem: A student prepares 100.0 cm³ of 0.200 mol dm⁻³ CuSO₄(aq) by placing 3.19 g of CuSO₄(s) in a 100.0 cm³ volumetric flask, dissolving it in some distilled water, adding distilled water to the mark and mixing. The concentration is later found to be less than 0.200 mol dm⁻³. Which of the following could explain this result?

options.text: The flask still held some distilled water from rinsing when the CuSO₄ was added.
Water was added until the bottom of the meniscus was above the mark.
Half of the solution was poured into a beaker before its concentration was measured.
The CuSO₄ dissolved completely, so no solid could be seen in the flask.

questions.explanation: Overfilling makes the volume more than 100.0 while the amount stays 0.0200 mol, so c = n/V falls.

questions.stem: 4-Oxopentanal, CH₃COCH₂CH₂CHO, has an aldehyde group and a ketone group. It is warmed with Tollens' reagent. What happens?

options.text: Both carbonyl groups are oxidised, so the product has two –COOH groups.
A silver mirror forms. Only the –CHO end is oxidised, to –COOH.
No silver mirror forms, because the ketone group stops the molecule being oxidised.
A silver mirror forms. The –CHO end is reduced to –CH₂OH, as the silver ions are.

questions.explanation: The aldehyde has an H on its carbonyl carbon, so it is oxidised: CH₃COCH₂CH₂COOH forms (as –COO⁻ in the alkaline reagent). The ketone group is unchanged.

questions.stem: Methyl orange can be written HInd(aq) ⇌ H⁺(aq) + Ind⁻(aq), with HInd red and Ind⁻ yellow. A few drops are added to aqueous ammonia: the solution is yellow. Hydrochloric acid is run in. Near the end it turns orange, then red. Why?

options.text: Added H⁺ shifts the indicator equilibrium to the right, so the red Ind⁻ form builds up.
Once the ammonia is used up, added H⁺ shifts the equilibrium left, so red HInd builds up.
The indicator reacts with the ammonium chloride formed, making a red salt.
The solution turns red at exactly pH 7, when the ammonia is neutralised.

questions.explanation: While NH₃ remains, it mops up the H⁺. Past equivalence [H⁺] jumps, the pH falls through methyl orange's range, and [HInd]/[Ind⁻] = [H⁺]/Ka becomes large.

questions.stem: Seawater contains about 1.29 g of magnesium ions, Mg²⁺, per dm³. How many moles of Mg²⁺ are in 250 cm³ of seawater? Data: Ar Mg 24.3.

options.text: 13.3 mol

questions.stem: Propanal is warmed with Tollens' reagent and a silver mirror forms. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Propanal is reduced to propan-1-ol, and the silver ions gain the hydrogen atoms.
Silver ions are oxidised to silver metal, and propanal is reduced.
Propanal is oxidised to propanoic acid, and silver ions are reduced to silver.
Propanal is oxidised to propanone, and silver ions are reduced to silver.

questions.explanation: CH₃CH₂CHO + [O] → CH₃CH₂COOH, while Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag. In the alkaline reagent the acid is present as the propanoate ion.

questions.stem: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ ammonia is titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid. Which indicator is the most suitable? Ranges: methyl orange 3.1–4.4; phenolphthalein 8.3–10.0; thymol blue 8.0–9.6; alizarin yellow 10.1–12.0.

options.text: phenolphthalein
methyl orange
thymol blue
alizarin yellow

questions.explanation: Strong acid + weak base: NH₄⁺ makes the equivalence point acidic (about pH 5.3), and the steep section runs down to about pH 3.5. Methyl orange changes there.

questions.stem: What amount of sodium hydroxide is present in 25.0 cm³ of NaOH(aq) in which [NaOH] = 0.100 mol dm⁻³?

options.text: 2.50 mol
